audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted their own why text: Level 2 read Ornn while whys[1] describes Sion winning the extended trade; Levels 4-5 and Level 6 read Skill while whys[3]/[4] describe Ornn knocking up an immobile Sion at will and calling 6 his strongest window; 2+ items read Ornn while whys[6] says it evens out.
audit.why: Sion is completely immobile — no dash anywhere in his kit — so Ornn's E-into-Q-pillar knock-up and R connect on him more reliably than on almost any top laner. Late, neither tank kills the other. The packet chart agrees with this reading on all four rows.
audit.corrected: Level 2 -> Skill, Levels 4-5 -> Ornn, Level 6 -> Ornn, 2+ items -> Skill, as matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 said only that 'Sion's ultimate changes the math'. Unstoppable Onslaught was never named or timed, and its rank scaling — the most dramatic in the matchup — went unmentioned.
audit.why: Unstoppable Onslaught is 140/100/60s. At rank 1 it trades roughly evenly with Ornn's 140s R; by rank 3 Sion has it more than twice as often. That is a genuine mid-game power shift and it belongs on the page.
audit.corrected: Named and timed in phases[4].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) The packet defect is real — no Sion ability was named anywhere on the page. (b) Decimating Smash was reduced to 'Charged = knockup. Dodge it.' with no cooldown and no statement that a quick release does not knock up at all. (c) Content text twice claims Sion's 'passive zombie state' helps him win level 1-2 trades; Glory in Death only triggers after Sion has been killed.
audit.why: Riot text, Q: 'If he charges for enough time, enemies hit by the swing will also be knocked up and stunned' — so a short-charge Q is damage plus slow, and reacting to charge duration is the actual skill. Riot text, P: 'After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate' — it is a death state, not a laning tool. Roar of the Slayer also shreds armour and knocks a minion back through you, which the page never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Ability names, the charge-duration rule, the 10s Q cooldown and the E armour shred now on the page; the false zombie-in-lane claim removed from whys[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: The anti-heal line was generic ('his healing fights your grind') and the build stacked raw resistances.
audit.why: Both flagged missing interactions apply. Glory in Death heals Sion off every rapid auto in his death state, so Grievous Wounds needs to exist BEFORE he first dies, not after. And Soul Furnace plus Glory in Death both deal damage scaled to the target's maximum health, so armour and MR stacking alone does not answer him.
audit.corrected: report[8] now times the anti-heal to his first death and names Glory in Death; phases[6].why states the %max-HP problem with resistance stacking.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Decimating Smash's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Sion is immobile, so E into your own Q pillar knocks him up every time. Decimating Smash is 10s at rank 1 — step in the moment he releases it.

edits.before: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — and your forge prints item leads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sion's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God's double knock-up locks a dashless Sion outright, and 6 is the time to use it: Unstoppable Onslaught is 140s at rank 1, only 60s at rank 3.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Sion carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two tanks who cannot solo-kill each other. Soul Furnace and Glory in Death deal %max HP — raw resistance stacking is not the answer.

edits.before: Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Only the full charge knocks up. 10s at rank 1 — step in when it is spent.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Soul Furnace is a shield that detonates after 3s for %max HP damage.

edits.before: Track Sion's Decimating Smash (Stun): Charged = knockup. Dodge it. When it is down — W-E + R him.
edits.after: Only a fully-charged Decimating Smash knocks up — a quick release is damage and a slow. It is 10s at rank 1.

edits.before: - Sion Decimating Smash: matchup-defining — Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sion Decimating Smash: 10s at rank 1, and only a full charge knocks up. - Roar of the Slayer: 12s — it shreds your armour and knocks a minion through you. - Unstoppable Onslaught: 140s at rank 1, 60s at rank 3.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (forge-upgradeable), then Sunfire Aegis; boots Plated Steelcaps. Add anti-heal (Thornmail component early) — his healing fights your grind.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (forge-upgradeable), then Sunfire Aegis; boots Plated Steelcaps. Get Grievous Wounds before he first dies — Glory in Death heals off every auto.

edits.before: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — build your teamfight around that. Sion carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — build your teamfight around that. Sion carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal before he dies, since Glory in Death heals through your chip.

edits.before: Still shieldless with only Q, while his passive zombie state and charged Q knockup let him win an extended trade.
edits.after: Only Q for you, and a fully-charged Decimating Smash knocks up — but it is 10s at rank 1, so neither of you commits.

notes: spikes[3].text also repeats the false 'passive zombie state' claim about levels 1-2 — I left it because rewriting it inside the 10% band without losing the (correct) rest of the sentence was not clean; flagging it here so it can be fixed in a follow-up. UNVERIFIED and left alone: the recurring claim that Bellows Breath is unstoppable and grants a shield (whys[2], early, mid, wants.you[1]) — Riot's W text says neither. Also unverified: whether Ornn's Q magma pillar stops or deflects Unstoppable Onslaught. Ornn's Q carries a terrain flag ('blocks paths and dashes') and Sion's R is a steered charge, so it is plausible and would be a high-value line, but Riot's R text only describes collision with an enemy, so I did not put it on the page.
